# Pascaal Console

> AI components for safety and adoption.

The Pascaal Console is the human control plane for Hallmark: organizations,
projects, scoped API keys, agents, grants, Freeroam traffic intelligence,
Trackline receipts, usage and billing.

**Status: UI preview only.** This console is a static prototype with mocked
data. It has no real authentication, database, API keys, key custody,
revocation service or billing. Do not enter real secrets.

## Read first

- Full product brief: /llms-full.txt
- Plain HTML agent view: /agent/
- Architecture rationale: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark/blob/main/docs/product-architecture.md
- Protocol site: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/
- Protocol llms.txt: https://hallmark.pascaal.com/llms.txt
- Company: https://pascaal.com/
- Source: https://github.com/Addyx2/hallmark

## What is real

- Hallmark Agent Identity Spec v1: open, executable, 21 sections, not ratified.
- Reference implementation: 38/38 spec-wide vectors, 4/4 properties, 4/4 enforcement points.
- `@pascaal/hallmark`, `@pascaal/freeroam`, `@pascaal/barricade`: draft product
  harness packages, staged locally, publish pending npm scope claim.
- Local provider demo + control room: runnable, in-memory only.

## What is preview only

- Signup/login, organizations, roles, projects, API keys, grants, traffic,
  receipts, usage and billing screens in this Console.
- "Create account" creates a new organization plus a starter project in preview
  memory. Roles (owner/admin/developer/viewer) are scoped per organization and
  enforced client-side only.
- All numbers, keys, agents and events shown here are mocked examples. Costs are
  mock cost units (100 units = $1); invoices are illustrative.

## Product vocabulary

- Imprint: signed root attestation binding a responsible human to an agent key.
- Grant: short-lived, per-action authority; has `jti`, `sqn`, budget, expiry.
- Freeroam: observe-only attribution middleware. Reads, records, never denies.
- Barricade: enforcement middleware on signed responsible-action surfaces.
- Trackline: PII-redacted receipt stream with pinned `HLM_` codes.
- Tenant (`hlm.tid`) + audience (`aud`): project isolation boundaries.

## Boundaries for agents

- Freeroam observes cooperative agent traffic and flags anomalies. It is not bot
  detection and it never denies a request.
- "Curb suspicious use" means Barricade checks an exact grant at the first
  responsible action (checkout, write, license, destructive operation).
- No remote key resolution. `jku`, `x5u` and `x5c` are forbidden by spec.
- No silent fail-open on stale revocation: grant surfaces fail closed.
- Do not call Hallmark ratified, certified or a standard until spec §21 closes.
- Conformance wording: "Hallmark v1-draft conformant — spec commit <sha>".
- No OpenAPI contract until the managed service exists. `docs/openapi.json` is
  deliberately deferred.

## Product status

- Hallmark: spec v1 open and executable.
- Plots: in design.
- Waterguard: research.

## Console surfaces

1. Signup and login — simulated, no password sent or stored.
2. Organizations and roles — owner, admin, developer, viewer.
3. Projects and API keys — scoped, hashed in production, shown once here.
4. Agents and grants — revoke a session or kill a lineage.
5. Traffic intelligence — observed usage, attribution, anomaly flags.
6. Trackline — filtered receipts; azp, ln and cnf each redacted by default and
   revealed together; export disabled in the preview.
7. Usage and billing — metered examples in cost units, differentiated plan
   tiers and illustrative invoices.
8. Docs for agents — this surface and its full brief.

The local provider demo can freeze its revocation manifest and advance a
simulated clock to demonstrate stale revocation failing closed with HLM_6004.
